datasets.title: Bank Marketing (bank-full)

expectations.note: Never-contacted structure: days_since_previous_campaign_contact = -1 on 36,954 rows, previous_campaign_outcome missing on 36,959, the two sets differing on 5 rows. On the file's original string form (missing marker kept as the literal 'NaN') a conditional rule reported this exactly; on the format-standard file (marker decoded to null) no detector reports it - measured in the standard profile, 2026-11-01. Tripwire: if a missingness-aware pass starts reporting it, this expectation fails and the case is promoted.
Format findings fire on this file (e.g. previous_campaign_outcome's value-length mix; terminal-digit preference on days_since_previous_campaign_contact from the -1 mass).

Overall subscription rate 11.7%. By previous-campaign outcome: success 64.7% (n = 1,511) vs failure 12.6%, other 16.7%, never-contacted 9.2% (n = 36,959). By month: mar 52.0% (n = 477) and dec 46.7% (n = 214) against may 6.7% (n = 13,766). Rates measured with Polars on the bundled file, 2026-11-01; recorded as documentation because the standard-budget run carries no target.

notes: Known-answer end of the business pack: heavily studied table, findings should be the documented structures.

Restandardized 2026-11-01 under the corpus format standard: descriptive file name, fully descriptive column names (pdays -> days_since_previous_campaign_contact, poutcome -> previous_campaign_outcome, ...), and the file's missing-value marker - the literal string "NaN": contact 28.8% (13,020 rows), previous_campaign_outcome 81.7% (36,959), education 4.1% (1,857), also a job level - decoded to null. Two expectations that were artifacts of the string form (the month=jun -> contact='NaN' rule and the matching hotspot) were retired with the decoding; the never-contacted rule is now a known-miss tripwire.
